To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of dipepeptidyl peptidase IV in the brush‐border membranes (BBMs) of the enterocytes of coeliac patients is significantly lower than that of normal subjects.
the brush‐border membrane enzyme DPP IV, which is expressed in the small intestine during development, is not expressed in the brush‐border membranes in children suffering from coelic disease.
the expression of dipeptide‐hydrolysing activity (DPP IV), but not disaccharide‐hydrolysing activities, is abnormal in the brush‐border membranes in coeliac disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the expression of brush‐border enzymes in the small intestinal mucosa of patients with coeliac disease.

the expression of brush‐border enzymes in enterocytes of coeliac children, which are shown to be abnormal, as well as with the possible relationship between the expression of DPP IV and the disaccharidases in the brush‐border membranes.
the abnormal development of enterocyte brush‐ border membranes in coeliac disease, which is characterized by a reduction in the time available for expression of the brush‐border membrane enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coeliac disease affects the expression of brush‐border membrane enzymes in enterocytes in a selective way.
DPP IV is not expressed in enterocyte brush borders during the first 3 months of life and then appears in the brush border at a normal level in the 3‐ to 6‐month period.
DPP IV activity in brush‐border membranes is abnormal in coeliac disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enterocyte brush‐borders of children with coeliac disease show a selective inhibition of DPP IV and disaccharidases.

in the enterocytes of children with coeliac disease, the brush‐border membrane is abnormal in the sense that it contains a decreased amount of the brush‐border enzyme DPP IV and that it has an abnormal capacity to synthesize disaccharidases.
the enterocytes of coeliac patients are unable to develop their brush‐border membrane enzymes to normal levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coeliac disease affects enterocytes in a highly specific way, and the effect on DPP IV is not a general one.
coeliac disease is a multifactorial disease that affects the entire digestive system.
coeliac disease inhibits the expression of DPP IV in the brush‐border membrane of enterocytes in children.
